description: Ofrezco un proyecto enfocado en una problemática clave para las futuras misiones a Marte (la basura orbital), combinado con una identidad creativa e innovadora (como nuestro concepto e imagen del quirquincho astronauta). Busco un entorno de trabajo colaborativo y enfocado en entregar una solución sólida.
summary: Project "Abandoned But Not Forgotten" introduces an innovative in-orbit recycling and repurposing platform designed to transform defunct satellites and orbital debris into valuable resources. Using autonomous robotic capture arms and modular processing units, the system intercepts space junk, strips functional components, and melts down structural metals for 3D printing new spacecraft components directly in microgravity. This approach mitigates the escalating Kessler syndrome threat in low Earth orbit, reduces the carbon footprint of rocket launches by enabling in-space manufacturing, and fosters a sustainable, circular orbital economy.
details:
Our web platform is designed to perform comprehensive tracking of space debris and inactive artifacts across Earth's orbit, the Moon, Mars, and deep space. Its purpose is to evaluate their accessibility in order to analyze the feasibility of reusing, recycling, or recovering their components and strategic metals (such as aluminum, titanium, and gold), promoting a circular economy in space exploration.

Regarding its benefits and impact, the project helps people understand the scale and management of space waste, a critical challenge for the future of aerospace exploration. It is aimed at both children and space enthusiasts, fostering early learning through pedagogical tools. Additionally, it offers an interactive experience that includes educational games for learning through play and a 3D map that tracks rovers, space stations, probes, satellites, and orbital debris.

For its development, we used tools such as JavaScript, JSON, and VS Code, relying on Copilot AI to streamline programming, and integrating official NASA APIs as our primary database to ensure accurate and reliable scientific information. On the creative side, it stands out as an interactive website that merges entertainment with research, transforming a complex issue into a playful, visual, and accessible platform for everyone.

Among the main factors we considered when designing the solution are: first, scientific rigor and technical feasibility through the use of open, real-world data from NASA; second, a focus on sustainability and a space circular economy, viewing debris in orbit, on the Moon, and on Mars as an opportunity to harness resources for future missions; third, pedagogical accessibility, adapting the interface so that both children and researchers find value; and fourth, intuitive 3D visualization so any user can gauge the location and status of objects in space in real time.
